logs.title: Shaping Convallaria's Core Loop
logs.description: Documenting the farming, combat, and death-as-growth ideas behind Convallaria while keeping the project direction focused and atmospheric.
logs.body: The current direction centers on a cozy farming RPG where progression is tied to legacy. Farming, exploration, and combat should all feed back into the world state instead of feeling like separate systems.
whatChanged: Defined the core loop around farming, exploration, combat, and legacy progression.
Clarified how death should change the next run instead of acting as a simple failure state.
Kept the visual direction cozy while preserving the darker Corpse Bloom / Afterbloom theme.
technicalNotes: Godot is the current target engine for rapid iteration on top-down systems.
The design needs persistent world-state data so later characters can react to earlier outcomes.
logs.comments: This is the north-star design note for Convallaria. Future implementation logs should connect back to this loop instead of drifting into isolated mechanics.

logs.title: Portfolio Activity Refresh
logs.description: Improved theme behavior, focus states, and smoother navigation so the portfolio feels cleaner without losing the simple static-site structure.
logs.body: This pass kept the portfolio lightweight while making the interaction details feel more intentional: focus rings, smooth scrolling, and clearer themed surfaces.
whatChanged: Moved repeated inline behavior into small JavaScript modules.
Added local JSON data for projects and manual dev logs.
Improved theme tokens, focus states, and GitHub-backed project activity.
technicalNotes: The site remains static and can be served with Python's built-in HTTP server.
Manual JSON data is the fallback when public GitHub API requests are rate-limited.
logs.comments: Manual dev logs should stay curated and readable. GitHub activity can support them, but it should not drown them out.

logs.title: MessApp Mobile Interaction Polish
logs.description: Focused on making realtime chat and calling behavior feel steadier on Android while keeping the interface readable and responsive.
logs.body: MessApp has grown into a practical realtime communication project: messages, attachments, calls, and mobile gestures all need to feel connected. This log captures the kind of work that matters most there: fixing rough interaction edges, tightening call teardown behavior, and preserving a smoother Android experience.
whatChanged: Improved mobile-first chat interaction expectations around message actions and overlays.
Focused call-state cleanup around answer/end flows so overlays do not linger.
Kept UI fixes close to the chat and call surfaces instead of broad rewrites.
technicalNotes: The app uses React, Supabase realtime state, Capacitor Android integration, and WebRTC media flows.
Manual validation is important because build success does not prove Android interaction behavior.
logs.comments: This is a good example of the kind of invisible engineering that makes an app feel finished: small interaction details, state cleanup, and mobile-specific acceptance testing.
